title: Banded Prefill/Decode Orchestrator — tenant fairbanding & kernel-aware split policy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a banded (multi-bucket) prefill/decode orchestrator that balances per-tenant latency SLOs and cluster throughput by assigning requests to dynamic bands based on latency targets, kernel cost hints, and attention window profiles. The orchestrator will: 1) compute a lightweight runtime 'band score' (latency_headroom, seq_len, kernel_hint, tenant_priority) per request; 2) map requests into bands (low-latency, balanced, cost-opt) with configurable capacity shards; 3) perform kernel-aware split points — i.e., prefer splitting prefill vs decode boundaries at positions that enable cheaper kernels or more efficient KV cache reuse; 4) expose per-tenant fairband quotas and temporal smoothing to avoid starvation; 5) integrate with existing hedging and opportunistic merging to reduce tail latency without sacrificing long-term fairness. This ticket focuses on the policy and runtime integration (not the full UI/Console controls).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by Infra and Runtime leads (link in 'links').
PoC scheduler implemented in single-node runtime harness with toggle flag --banded-orchestrator.
Benchmarks show <=10% median latency regression for low-latency band and >=8% cost reduction for cost band on mixed synthetic workload compared to baseline 1.19 scheduler.
Integration tests cover kernel-hint propagation and KV cache correctness across split points.
Canary plan documented and rollout guardrails added to console release notes.
discussion: 2026-02-28 Asha: Kickoff - captured initial goals and measured current cluster distributions from datadog (dd/dashboard/runtime-prefill).
2026-03-02 Marco: Prototype of band score calculator (see PR #1249) — uses sequence length quantiles + cached kernel cost table from kernel-probe service.

2026-03-04 Review (Infra): Concern about KV cache invalidation when splitting across model sharding boundary; proposed solution is to prefer split offsets aligned to KV shard boundaries or to replicate small prefixes.
2026-03-06 Design feedback (Applied ML): Attention-window hints need attenuation for instruction-tuned models — added scale factor in band score formula.
2026-03-09 Eng pairing: Implemented temporal smoothing (exponential moving average) for per-tenant band assignments to reduce oscillation under bursty load.
2026-03-11 QA: Found race where hedging combines with band migration leading to double-counted tokens in billing; added billing consistency check in runtime path.
decisions: Use three bands by default: low-latency (strict SLO), balanced (default), cost-optimized (aggressive batching/quant kernels).
Kernel hints are advisory and encoded in request metadata; runtime may override on capacity constraints.
Split points will prefer offsets that increase KV cache reuse or switch to cheaper attention kernels (e.g., sliding-window) where available.
Per-tenant fairband quotas will be enforced as soft limits with immediate throttling only for P0 tenants; others receive gradual demotion to lower bands.
Hedging remains enabled for low-latency band but hedged requests inherit same band-level quotas to avoid work amplification on cost band.
next_steps: Finish PoC and attach microbench results for 4 synthetic mixes (chatty short, long-context decode, embeddings-heavy, mixed traffic).
Implement runtime guardrail that prevents split offsets crossing KV-shard boundaries unless explicitly forced by override flag.
Add telemetry metrics: band_assignment, band_queue_time, kernel_used_at_split, kv_cache_reuse_rate, per-tenant_band_violations.
Create canary rollout: 5% of traffic in us-east-1 to start, monitor latency SLO & cost metrics for 72h before 25% expansion.
Sync with Product to define Console controls for band quotas and an API flag for customers to request low-latency band (billing implications).
